title: vault-meta-ntv8 — case shape (v0.2)
description: Pins the NTV8 vault.meta generation: the NTV6 frame byte for byte (magic NTV8, protocol_version 0x02, reserved 0x00, the 345-byte base, the group-key package, the epoch and the sealed roster) and NOTHING after the roster. The absence of the person wrap is the length, not a zeroed block: 445 + roster_len with any other length invalid, so a later writer cannot relax it without changing the number every parser compares against. The three recovery-phrase wrap fields (recovery salt at offset 49, recovery nonce at 153, recovery-wrapped root_key at 177) MUST be all zero in both directions, exactly as on NTV7 — they are kept rather than compacted away because their offsets belong to the shared §9.3 base layout, and removing them would move items_key_id and the itemsKey wrap, turning a truncation of one frame into a re-wrap of every vault. The master password is the only vault credential: the identity phrase is an identity, and it opens nothing here. Also pins the NTV7 to NTV8 upgrade, which is the same bytes with the 1208-byte person envelope removed and the magic rewritten — no key re-wrapped, so the password a user already has still opens the file, carried as one case that supplies both the expected bytes and the root_key they open to. Reference implementation: protocol/src/vault_meta_ntv8.rs (main myne repository).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-meta-ntv8/v0.2/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

oneOf.title: roundtrip — parse then re-serialize is byte-identical

input_blob_hex.description: The whole frame. Length must be 445 + roster_len.

expected_blob_hex.description: What a parse-then-serialize must reproduce exactly. Equal to input_blob_hex for a valid frame; the separate field is what makes the assertion explicit rather than a port re-echoing its input.

expected_signed_roster_len.description: The u32 BE roster length at offset 441; the roster itself starts at 445 and ends the frame.

expected_base_account_number_hash_hex.description: Base field at offset 6, read through the generation-agnostic base reader.

expected_kdf_m_kib.description: The frame's own Argon2id memory cost. Pinned because a port that ignores the frame's parameters and uses its own defaults derives a different wrap key while parsing every byte correctly — the same trap the `password_opens` case catches from the other side.

expected_kdf_argon2_version.description: 0x13 (19) on every frame this reference implementation writes.

expected_phrase_wrap_zeroed.description: The three retired phrase-wrap fields must be all zero. Structural, not a flag.

expected_person_wrap_absent.description: No person envelope after the roster. The length is what says so.

oneOf.title: password_opens — the frame opens to one root key under the master password

input_password_utf8_hex.description: The password's UTF-8 bytes, verbatim: this path performs no normalization, and a port that applies one derives a different wrap key.

expected_root_key_hex.description: The 32-byte vault root_key. Carried so a mismatch names which half diverged: a wrong frame fails the parse, a wrong root key fails the salt domain, the AAD role or the KDF block.

oneOf.title: password_open_fail — a wrong password fails closed

informational_reason.description: Informational only: the refusal is ONE non-distinguishing AEAD failure (§6.4), so a port must not distinguish a wrong password from a tampered frame.

oneOf.title: upgrade — an NTV7 frame becomes the NTV8 frame, re-wrapping nothing

expected_blob_hex.description: The NTV8 frame it must become: the same bytes with the person envelope removed and the magic rewritten to NTV8. Every byte from offset 4 to the end of the roster is IDENTICAL to the input's, which is the whole claim: the upgrade truncates, it does not re-wrap.

expected_dropped_person_wrap_len.description: ML-KEM ciphertext (1088) || classical ephemeral Ed25519 public key (32) || AEAD nonce (24) || wrapped root_key (64).

expected_root_key_hex.description: The SAME root key the NTV7 frame opens to under the same password. A port that re-wraps the root key during the upgrade produces a frame this password no longer opens, and this field is what fails.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — a structural rejection the frame must refuse

informational_reason.description: Which rule this case trips. Informational only: the rejection is deliberately ONE non-distinguishing result, so a port must not surface the reason.
